fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. The text says, "the king is captured in your tresses." (Song of Solomon 7:5) The shepherd isn't named in this line. Here it's the king who gets caught.
Good guess, friend. But this verse says, "the king is captured in your tresses." (Song of Solomon 7:5) The watchman isn't named here. The king is the one caught.

I can see why you'd pick it, friend. Here she says something different: "I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me." (Song of Solomon 7:10) No waiting in this line. She says she is his and he wants her.
Not this one, friend. In this line she says, "I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me." (Song of Solomon 7:10) She isn't looking for him here. She's telling who she belongs to.
Right, friend. She says, "Come, my beloved, let us go to the countryside; let us spend the night among the wildflowers." (Song of Solomon 7:11) She's the one doing the inviting here.
Yes, friend. She wants to see "…if the vine has budded, if the blossom has opened, if the pomegranates are in bloom…" (Song of Solomon 7:12) She names the vine, the blossom and the pomegranates.

That's a good thought, friend, but it isn't what she says. She wants to see "…if the vine has budded, if the blossom has opened…" (Song of Solomon 7:12) It's buds and blossoms she names, not ripe grapes.

Not at this door, friend. She says, "…at our door is every delicacy, new as well as old, that I have treasured up for you, my beloved." (Song of Solomon 7:13) No message is mentioned. It's delicacies she saved for him.
